scaled_2d_obstacle_recovery.description: Scaled nonlinear 2D obstacle recovery benchmark mirroring the paper's unicycle complex-constraint recovery protocol.
scaled_2d_obstacle_recovery.notes: Paper values are the reported unicycle g3 recovery accuracies from Sec. 4.2. The gym uses a CPU-feasible scaled 2D boundary-band analogue with the same safe/unsafe recovery objective and equal demonstration-budget constraint.

n_demos.description: Number of requested demonstrations, penalizing methods that improve classification only by using a larger query budget.

_scale_note: Paper setting restored where it was specified: 2D double integrator at dt=1, T=30, squared successive-position cost, workspace [-15,15]^2 (the paper's g3 figures), the paper's g3 polynomial, 1000 RFF, alpha 0.3, delta 0.001, beta 0.55/0.3/0.55. KKT gradient estimates, identified only up to a positive per-state scale (App. A.1), enter the GP as unit-norm directions. GP hyperparameters minimize the cited Chou et al. (2022) Sec. IV-B loss (negative marginal log likelihood plus the demonstration-feasibility hinge on mean+rho*sd, rho=0.1), with the observation-noise variance bounded below by 1e-4 (GPyTorch's inferred-noise floor; chosen on the development split among 1e-4, 1e-5 and 1e-6, replacing a numerically singular 1e-10); the constant prior mean is tied to -rho*signal so unexplored states have prior safety probability Phi(0.1)=0.54 < beta=0.55. The paper's own zero-mean posterior (Eqs. 15-16) was tested as the reference and rejected on the development split by a rule fixed in advance: its uniform accuracy collapsed to 0.73 (0.97 tied). Eq. 10 is the prose's safe probability Phi(-mean/sd)>=beta. Problem 3 is solved over the sampled boundary within one fitted lengthscale of observed tight states. Benchmark choices the paper leaves unspecified (selected on the development split only): four shared initial crossing demonstrations, twelve demonstrations and forty start/goal requests per instance for every method, Alg. 1 iterated with a refit after every batch of P=4 posterior draws until the budget is spent, eta=1. Instances add random rotation, scale in [0.88,1.08], centre offsets in [-2,2]^2 and a smooth radial deformation of the g3 shape (different private families on development and test, RMS about 4% of the radius). The complex-boundary stress shapes likewise use a different private family on the hidden test, matched to development in radius variation (RMS 0.140 vs 0.141 of the mean radius), boundary slope and narrowest radius. Seventy-two paired hidden instances per double-integrator experiment (twenty-four on development). The paper's main-text experiments are added: unicycle (App. B.1 g1, g2, g3; 4D unicycle dynamics, dt=1, T=30, [-15,15]^2) and quadrotor (hourglass g5; 12D quadrotor, dt=1, T=20, [-6,6]^3), with 72 and 96 hidden instances (24 and 24 on development), the same 4 shared crossings + 12-demonstration / 40-request budget, and private per-instance rotation, scale (0.88-1.08), translation and smooth displacement-field deformation (RMS about 0.3 (2D) and 0.39 (3D) shape units; a different field family on development). The expert solves Prob. 1 exactly in position space (unbounded controls and free non-position endpoint states place no restriction on positions) and lifts each path to the full state/control trajectory; the reference solves Probs. 7-8 as linear programs over the full KKT system of each system's dynamics. Weights: unicycle 0.35, quadrotor 0.25, double-integrator g3 0.2, complex-boundary 0.2. Boundary-band metrics and the complex-boundary stress experiment extend the paper's uniform-sample accuracy. Original reported numbers remain in _paper_reported_* and are not targets at this scale; split-specific benchmark measurements are kept separately under _measured_reference_runs.
